Spiced Wine Hypocras

Served at: Feast of the Ass

Serves 6Prep 10 minCook 15 min

Spiced Wine Hypocras is a traditional medieval festive drink often served during the Feast of the Ass, a celebration held on January 14th commemorating the biblical journey of Mary and Joseph. This warm, aromatic wine is infused with spices and sweetened with honey, embodying the rich flavors and convivial spirit of the holiday.

Ingredients

  • 1 bottle (750 ml) red wine, such as Merlot or Cabernet Sauvignon
  • 1/4 cup (85 g) honey
  • 1 cinnamon stick
  • 5 whole cloves
  • 3 whole allspice berries
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger
  • 1/4 teaspoon freshly grated nutmeg
  • 1 vanilla bean, split lengthwise
  • 1 strip of orange peel (avoid white pith)

Method

  1. Pour the red wine into a medium saucepan over low heat.
  2. Add the honey, cinnamon stick, cloves, allspice berries, ground ginger, grated nutmeg, vanilla bean, and orange peel to the wine.
  3. Warm the mixture gently, stirring occasionally, until it is hot but not boiling (about 15 minutes).
  4. Remove the saucepan from heat and let the wine steep with the spices for 30 minutes to an hour for deeper flavor.
  5. Strain the wine through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth to remove the spices and solids.
  6. Serve warm in heatproof glasses or mugs.

Tips

  • Do not boil the wine to preserve its delicate flavors and alcohol content.
  • For a festive touch, garnish each serving with a cinnamon stick or a twist of orange peel.
  • You can adjust the sweetness by adding more or less honey according to taste.
